I lived in Japan. It's pretty dull -- and pretty big. The western focus on Harajuku is a bit like an imaginary Asian focus on Burning Man. The conformist stereotype is closer to the norm. At the same time, Japanese can be weird to Asians -- but often in their adherence to tradition. Chinese will praise tradition, only to blithely ignore it. Japanese often have a better idea of their cultural heritage but have mixed feelings about sharing. The "weirdest" things can be pretty well founded and handled with kid gloves. In Asia, I've seen the opinion that the most shocking things are Chinese, the most... spectacular? are Japanese. The "bizarroland" tends to be the edges of Asia: Philippines, Indonesia..., but these differences are considered "un-Asian" and also "interesting".

Clips of Japanese TV are often anomalous -- and sometimes from porn movies. A lot of .jp TV is pretty formulaic. With a touch of .jp, you can fill in the interviews. The game shows always have a team of four: the "game girl/guy", the over-reactor, the "too cool for school", and average joe. The food is pretty normal in combinis. (If you hate "weird", you can rely on Seven to provide a normalized backdrop wherever you go.)

That said, it can be an interesting place -- within bounds. If you like history (or buddhism), there's plenty. If you like salty snacks and public parties, go shinto. There's plenty of trains and a public interest in train lines. (I strongly suspect there's trainspotters, but I've never seen it...)
